Stepwise regression

Source: R/ols-stepwise-regression.R
ols_step_both_p.Rd

Build regression model from a set of candidate predictor variables by entering and removing predictors based on p values, in a stepwise manner until there is no variable left to enter or remove any more.

Usage

ols_step_both_p(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
ols_step_both_p(
  model,
  p_enter = 0.1,
  p_remove = 0.3,
  include = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  progress = FALSE,
  details = FALSE,
  steps = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'ols_step_both_p'
plot(x, model = NA, print_plot = TRUE, details = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

model

An object of class lm; the model should include all candidate predictor variables.

...

Other arguments.

p_enter

p value; variables with p value less than p_enter will enter into the model.

p_remove

p value; variables with p more than p_remove will be removed from the model.

include

Character or numeric vector; variables to be included in selection process.

exclude

Character or numeric vector; variables to be excluded from selection process.

progress

Logical; if TRUE, will display variable selection progress.

details

Logical; if TRUE, will print the regression result at each step.

steps

Number of steps after which the stepwise procedures should stop.

x

An object of class ols_step_both_p.

print_plot

logical; if TRUE, prints the plot else returns a plot object.

Value

ols_step_both_p returns an object of class "ols_step_both_p". An object of class "ols_step_both_p" is a list containing the following components:

model

final model; an object of class lm

metrics

selection metrics

beta_pval

beta and p values of models in each selection step

Details

Refits accept explicit contrast matrices or the base contrast names contr.treatment, contr.sum, contr.helmert, contr.poly and contr.SAS (resolved from the stats namespace); models fitted with custom named contrast functions must be refitted with an explicit matrix, for example contrasts = list(g = my_matrix). Refits carry the fitted model's frozen total offset as an argument with all formula offset() terms removed for standardized-beta and selection computations. Returned stepwise models are fitted from the original call, preserving formula and argument offsets for prediction on new data. Their coefficients, fitted values and total offset must be identical to the frozen-offset selection fit; otherwise selection stops with an error because prediction with new data is not supported for that model.

For non-hierarchical stepwise selection, candidate rankings and criterion improvement tests use 10 significant digits: values that agree to 10 significant digits are ties, equal criterion values mean no improvement, and a remaining tie goes to the first candidate in formula order after any F tie is broken by p value (smaller for entry, larger for removal). P-value entry and removal cutoffs are compared without rounding.

References

Chatterjee, Samprit and Hadi, Ali. Regression Analysis by Example. 5th ed. N.p.: John Wiley & Sons, 2012. Print.

Examples

# \donttest{
# stepwise regression
model <- lm(y ~ ., data = surgical)
ols_step_both_p(model)
#> 
#> 
#>                                 Stepwise Summary                                
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Step    Variable             AIC        SBC       SBIC        R2       Adj. R2 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#>  1      liver_test (+)     771.875    777.842    616.009    0.45454    0.44405 
#>  2      alc_heavy (+)      761.439    769.395    605.506    0.56674    0.54975 
#>  3      enzyme_test (+)    750.509    760.454    595.297    0.65900    0.63854 
#>  4      pindex (+)         735.715    747.649    582.943    0.75015    0.72975 
#>  5      bcs (+)            730.620    744.543    579.638    0.78091    0.75808 
#> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> Final Model Output 
#> ------------------
#> 
#>                            Model Summary

# stepwise regression plot
model <- lm(y ~ ., data = surgical)
k <- ols_step_both_p(model)
plot(k)


# selection metrics
k$metrics
#>   step    variable   method        r2    adj_r2      aic      sbc     sbic
